chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The practices of doing good protect from the falls of evil, and every good deed is charity. Those who do good in this world are the doers of good in the Hereafter, and those who do evil in this world are the doers of evil in the Hereafter. Indeed, the first of the inhabitants of Paradise to enter Paradise are those who do good, and the first of the people of Hell to enter Hell are those who do evil.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of doing good deeds according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) emphasizes that consistent good deeds (sanā'i' al-ma'rūf) serve as a shield against ruin, with every act of kindness considered charity. The text establishes a direct correlation between one's actions in this world and their status in the Hereafter, noting that the 'doers of good' will be the first to enter Paradise, while the 'doers of evil' will be the first to enter Hell. This hadith highlights the Shia concept of 'tawassul' through good character, where social benevolence becomes a spiritual merit that accelerates one's entry into the divine presence.
